decision.summary: Tenant emailed one month's notice for 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act two months is required, so the earliest valid end is 10 Dec 2026. I acknowledged this to the tenant, asked the landlord whether he accepts 10 Nov in writing, and started move-out against 10 Dec.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: Not as to the date. Written notice is accepted, but one month is too short; two months is needed. Given 10 Oct 2026, the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date (e.g. 10 Nov); a surrender by mutual agreement. The agency cannot agree this itself. Landlord asked via APR-102.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied (MSG-101) giving the 10 Dec date, explaining early end needs landlord's written agreement, keys to be returned at checkout with details to follow, deposit returned via mydeposits after checkout with ADR for disputes, returned within 10 days of agreement. Started: landlord request, chase follow-up 14 Oct, and checkout/key-return follow-up 10 Dec.

actions_claimed.description: Replied to tenant acknowledging notice and explaining end date, keys, deposit
Asked landlord whether he accepts 10 Nov and told him of move-out steps
Follow-up 10 Dec for checkout inspection and key return

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; law requires two months.
assumptions: Email counts as written notice, served 10 Oct 2026.
Periodic tenancy so two months applies; rent due on 1st continues to end date.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email of 10 October, which we have received as your written notice to leave Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road. Congratulations on the new job.

Under the current rules a tenant needs to give two months' notice, not one. Your earliest valid end date is therefore 10 December 2026, and your tenancy and rent continue until then. We cannot shorten that ourselves: it can only end sooner if your landlord agrees in writing. We are asking him today whether he will accept 10 November, and we'll let you know his answer. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you hear from us in writing.

Keys: we'll arrange a checkout inspection near your end date and tell you the time and exactly where and how to hand the keys back. Please don't leave them anywhere before then.

Deposit: your £2,019 is protected with mydeposits. After checkout, any proposed deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's independent dispute service if we can't agree. It is returned within 10 days of agreement.

We'll be in touch again by 17 October with the landlord's answer and checkout plans.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
